motion.name: reveal
motion.value: opacity 0 to 1, translateY 30px to 0, 500ms ease-out, once, 50px into view
motion.purpose: Every section and card on scroll.

motion.name: reveal-stagger
motion.value: 100ms per sibling; 30ms to 50ms for chips and characters
motion.purpose: Sibling delay inside a revealed group.

motion.name: world-switch
motion.value: quick-change curtain 600ms to 800ms in the incoming world's exit gesture; 300ms View Transition crossfade under reduced motion or as fallback
motion.purpose: Switching designs.

motion.name: hover-color
motion.value: 150ms
motion.purpose: Color and border transitions on links, chips, and cards.

motion.name: hover-lift
motion.value: translateY(-4px); Creative buttons scale(1.05); Creative chips scale(1.1)
motion.purpose: Cards and Creative interactive elements.

motion.name: dropdown
motion.value: 150ms, opacity 0 to 1, y -8px to 0, scale 0.95 to 1
motion.purpose: Design switcher list.

motion.name: mobile-panel
motion.value: 300ms tween from translateX(100%); backdrop 200ms fade
motion.purpose: Mobile navigation.

motion.name: pager-print
motion.value: each first-page block appears outright (10ms opacity) 45ms after the last, from 50ms
motion.purpose: Engineer hero: the pager draws the screen top to bottom; no fade, no rise.

motion.name: session-replay
motion.value: 26ms per character, 70ms after a command, 55ms after output, from 120ms; block cursor blinks at 1.1s steps(2)
motion.purpose: Terminal hero: the server renders the finished session, hydration replays it; reduced motion keeps it finished and the cursor steady.

motion.name: tape-feed
motion.value: band x 35% to 0 over 900ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); window rises 24px over 500ms; flag drops 12px at 800ms
motion.purpose: Tape hero.

motion.name: char-stagger
motion.value: 30ms per character, 400ms each, y 40px
motion.purpose: Avant-garde hero name.

motion.name: word-stagger
motion.value: 150ms per word from 150ms, 600ms each, y 60px; the rule, role, employer line, tagline, and actions follow within 150ms to 500ms without a stagger
motion.purpose: Editorial hero name, the only staggered element, so the role is legible in about 0.7s.

motion.name: parallax
motion.value: name -80px, subtitle -40px across the hero scroll
motion.purpose: Editorial hero.

motion.name: rule-draw
motion.value: scaleX 0 to 1 from the left, 800ms
motion.purpose: Avant-garde and Editorial hero rules; Editorial hairlines, including the one opening each news item.

motion.name: marquee
motion.value: translateX 0 to -50%, 30s linear infinite
motion.purpose: Avant-garde capability band.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: CSS animation and transition durations 0.01ms, smooth scroll off; Motion MotionGlobalConfig.skipAnimations = true (src/lib/reduced-motion.ts), so JS animations jump to their end state
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: intro-curtain
motion.value: 1.5s to 1.9s per world, fonts awaited up to 700ms except Editorial (data-intro-no-font-wait; its rule is a stub on frame one); heroes hydrate as the exit begins (0.95s to 1.35s)
motion.purpose: Arrival on the home's first hard load of the session (sessionStorage key intro-seen, set in BaseLayout's inline script); deep links, later loads, in-site navigation, and reduced motion skip it; click, Escape, a wheel, or a swipe over it ends it.

motion.name: cursor-hover-scale
motion.value: ring scale 1 to 1.5 (32px to 48px) eased 0.2 per frame; ring follows the native cursor with a 0.15 lerp
motion.purpose: Avant-garde cursor ring over links and buttons on fine pointers; transform only, no re-layout; the native cursor stays visible.

motion.name: no-js
motion.value: <noscript> style: elements whose inline style starts at opacity 0 or scaleX(0) forced to opacity 1, transform none; a hero island that throws renders HeroFallback (name, role, CV, email)
motion.purpose: Keeps Motion's server-rendered start states (Editorial's rule included) and failed hero islands from hiding the page.

motion.name: curtains-new-worlds
motion.value: Engineer reveal 1.25s / total 1.3s (pages back from (END) every 85ms from 0.7s; quick 0.55s: every 50ms from 0.2s); Terminal reveal 1.3s, lifts on site-hero:ready, cap 2.2s (quick: lifts at 0.45s or on site-hero:ready, cap 1.2s); Tape reveal 0.4s (hero hydrates underneath, already in place), fades 0.35s when the reader is done (~1.35s after the font wait), cap 2.6s (quick: role burst, fade 0.28s, cap 1.4s)
motion.purpose: Arrival and quick-change timing for Engineer, Terminal, and Tape in SiteIntro.astro.

motion.name: cartoon-on-twos
motion.value: steps(1, end) keyframes held per pose; cartoon-drop 0.36s (letters, 45ms apart from 0.1s), cartoon-pop 0.44s at 0.15s (painter), cartoon-disc 0.3s at 0.08s, cartoon-roll steps(6) 0.5s at 0.45s (band), rest steps(2) 0.24s from 0.3s; ticket hover steps(2) 0.16s rotate(-2deg)
motion.purpose: Cartoon hero entrance and hovers: limited animation, never tweened.

motion.name: cartoon-view-titles
motion.value: animation-timeline: view(); letters entry 10% + i*3% to 45% + i*3%; the peek pops entry 45% to 85%
motion.purpose: Cartoon section titles drop in letter by letter as each card scrolls in, then the caricature pops up.

motion.name: cartoon-boil
motion.value: three SVG ink filters cycled 0.42s steps(1); eyes blink 5.2s from 2.4s; wave 3.6s on held poses
motion.purpose: The caricature's line boil, blink, and wave (off under reduced motion).

motion.name: cartoon-iris
motion.value: @property --cartoon-iris 75vmax to min(42vw, 15rem), view() entry 0% to cover 55%
motion.purpose: The footer's iris closes on THE END as the page runs out.

motion.name: cartoon-curtain
motion.value: leader card lettered in, cut at 0.95s; iris opens 1.0s to 1.6s cubic-bezier(0.55, 0, 0.8, 0.35) centred on the painter's face (cartPlace); reveal 1s, total 1.65s (quick: no card, iris 0.2s to 0.7s, total 0.75s)
motion.purpose: Cartoon's intro curtain and quick-change in SiteIntro.astro.

motion.name: clay-on-twos
motion.value: clay-pop 0.34s steps(1, end), hero lines from 0.05s to 0.5s (paused while the curtain is up); set canvas clay-lights 0.25s steps(2); keycap press translate only, 0.2s steps(2) (hover a third of --depth, active two thirds); tool keys 2px, 0.16s steps(2); folder squash 0.25s steps(3); running commit clay-live 1s steps(1) Mint to Side Mint
motion.purpose: Clay: stop-motion, poses held, never tweened.

motion.name: clay-plop
motion.value: scale(1.03, 0.95) to (0.98, 1.03) to (1.01, 0.99) to none, 0.34s steps(1, end), when 25% of a window is on screen; never hidden first
motion.purpose: Clay: each editor window plops into place.

motion.name: clay-set-12fps
motion.value: react-three-fiber frameloop demand invalidated every 1000/12 ms; mounted only while Clay is the active world (MutationObserver on html data-design unmounts the canvas); paused off screen (IntersectionObserver) or under reduced motion (one still frame); dpr [1, 2], [1, 1.5] and a 1024px shadow map below 768px
motion.purpose: Clay hero's live Three.js set, shot on twos; the FPS meter reads 12 FPS, 83 ms.

motion.name: clay-still
motion.value: sprite sheet, steps(frames, jump-none) over frames/12 s, infinite; first frame under reduced motion
motion.purpose: Clay: Akira's wave (8 frames, the footer) and point (3 frames, Contact).

motion.name: clay-curtain
motion.value: </> rolled out in three lit coils (Pink, Orange, Purple) clay-coil-in 0.3s steps(1) at 0.08s, 0.2s, 0.32s; name at 0.44s; glyph squashed and lifted clay-glyph-out 0.4s steps(1) at 0.72s; sweep cut at 1.05s; reveal 0.95s, total 1.2s (quick: glyph already there, no name, out at 0.12s, sweep cut 0.5s, total 0.7s)
motion.purpose: Clay's intro curtain and quick-change in SiteIntro.astro, drawn in the world's tokens (--bg, --clay-*).

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Repertoire"**

One performer, nine staged productions of the same script. The content (name, title, tagline, experience, skills, projects, blog) never changes; a switch in the header restages it in one of nine complete visual worlds: Editorial (the default), Avant-garde, Engineer, Creative, Arcade, Terminal, Tape, Cartoon, and Clay. The system's personality is plural on purpose. Each world commits fully to its own register (the broadsheet, the dark gallery, the Internet-Draft read in a pager, the studio, the arcade cabinet, the shell session, the punched teletype tape, the opening titles of a 1960s cartoon, and a developer's desk moulded in plasticine). None of them is a theme laid over a neutral base, because the neutral base does not exist.

Underneath, one skeleton carries all nine: a fixed translucent header, a full-viewport hero, and a single centered column of sections (About, Experience, Education, Skills, Projects, Contact) at medium density. A world declares nine semantic color tokens (page, raised, text, secondary text, accent, accent hover, border, card, card hover), two font slots, and two radii, and the shared sections re-skin themselves. Two accent-use tokens sit on top for every world: `--on-accent`, the text on an accent fill (the page color by default), and `--accent-text`, small text in the accent (the accent itself by default); a world overrides either only when its accent needs it, as Editorial and Engineer do. A world may add tokens of its own beside the nine when its material needs them (Terminal's prompt green and bright text, Tape's punched windows, Cartoon's five paper fields, Clay's five clays and its surface tile); they never leave that world. Every world stages its own Hero, Experience, and Skills; Editorial, Engineer, Terminal, Tape, Cartoon, and Clay also stage their own About and footer, and the last five their own Education, Projects, and Contact.

The aesthetic philosophy is restraint everywhere except the accent and the display type. Every world spends its accent on small, high-signal things: buttons, period labels, rules, hover and selection states. Cartoon turns the strategy over: colour is the field, not the accent; every section is a title card drenched in one of five flat paper colours, and on each card the accent is the one colour that card names safe for small text. Clay keeps one field, the painted teal sweep, and puts its colour in the clay laid on it; its pink accent is only ever a fill with ink on it, never text. Display typography carries identity, except in Engineer, where one face at one size carries it and hierarchy comes from numbering, position, indent, and bold. Motion is one shared reveal grammar (fade and rise on scroll, once) plus a single signature per world, staged in the hero and in its curtain; Cartoon and Clay replace the tween with poses held on twos.
keyCharacteristics: Nine complete worlds, one content source, switched at runtime and persisted per visitor.
One accent per world, spent on interactive and labeling elements only; Terminal's prompt green is its one sanctioned second voice.
Display typography carries identity: monospace, typewriter, geometric sans, heavy grotesk, display grotesk, slab poster, condensed caps, hand-lettered cartoon titling, or letters rolled from clay.

Flat surfaces in seven worlds: border-defined in six, drenched cut-paper fields in Cartoon, where depth is only paper lying on paper. Two worlds lift: Creative with a soft neutral shadow, Clay with lit, shaded plasticine that casts a soft teal shadow on its sweep.
Shared reveal motion (fade, 30px rise, 0.5s, once) with a signature per world, staged in the hero.

WebGL in two worlds: Avant-garde's particle field, mounted only while that world is active and backed by a CSS fallback, and Clay's live tabletop set, likewise mounted only while Clay is active, rendered at 12 frames a second on demand and paused off screen.
Candy stays on the cards: Arcade's candy colors are surfaces, never UI chrome. Cartoon's fields are surfaces too, one per section; Clay's clays are material, laid on the sweep.
Limited animation in Cartoon and Clay: poses held on twos (`steps()`), never tweened.
Bilingual by construction: every text node renders both locales and CSS shows one.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Each world has exactly one accent and spends it on buttons, labels, rules, hover and selection states. Body copy, headings, and card surfaces never take the accent. Arcade's candy colors are surfaces with Cabinet Black text on them, never accents. Terminal's prompt green is the shell's own prompt colour, held to the prompt user, active periods, JSON values, and the email key; it never becomes a second link or hover colour. Cartoon's fields are surfaces, like the candy; on each card the accent is the one safe colour that card names.

rules.name: The Own Palette Rule
rules.body: A world uses only its own token set, world-only tokens included. No Candy Green in Engineer, no Creative shadow in Editorial, no Tape Orange in Editorial or Signal Orange in Tape, no prompt green outside the terminal, no Cartoon field outside Cartoon, no clay outside Clay.

rules.name: The Dark Text on Bright Accent Rule
rules.body: Text on an accent fill reads `--on-accent`; small text in the accent reads `--accent-text`. Lime, Gold, and Tape Orange are light accents, so their fills take the page color, the default (6.3:1 to 16:1); Terminal's green key takes Terminal Ground (7.45:1). Violet's own hero and filter fills take white (6.7:1), and Engineer sets `--on-accent` to white on Link Blue (6.70:1). Signal Orange measures 3.0:1 on Newsprint and 3.3:1 under white text, so Editorial sets `--on-accent` to Ink (5.2:1) and `--accent-text` to Signal Orange Ink (#bf3900, 4.5:1 or more on every Editorial surface); in Editorial, `.text-accent`, `hover:text-accent`, and `group-hover:text-accent` all render in it. Raw Signal Orange stays on rules, outlines, fills, and text at 24px and up, which opts in through `.text-accent-display`. Clay Pink fails even display size on the sweep (1.02:1), so Clay sets both tokens and `.text-accent-display` to Clay Ink.

rules.name: The Reverse Video Rule (Engineer)
rules.body: Engineer has two fills and no others: the blue Email key and reverse video (Ink fill, Cool Paper text). Reverse video marks what a pager would highlight: standalone figures in the copy (`.rfc-mark`, split out by `src/lib/figures.ts`, like `less` search matches), the pinned status line, and its "(END)".

rules.name: The Window Ink Rule (Tape)
rules.body: Running copy sits in punched White windows in Tape Black ink. Orange never sets text inside a window (2.79:1); there it only underlines and rules. Orange text lives on the black ground.

rules.name: The Field Rule (Cartoon)
rules.body: Every card names four colours: its field (`--field`), its text (`--on-field`), a safe colour for small text, focus rings, and hovers (`--safe`, 4.5:1 or more on the field), and a display colour for large type only (`--hi`). The card re-points `--text`, `--text-secondary`, `--accent`, `--accent-text`, `--on-accent`, `--border`, and Tailwind's `--color-*` utilities to them, so shared islands re-skin per card. Paper on Vermilion (3.4:1) is display only, never running text. A new card takes only one of the measured pairs.

rules.name: The Ink on Clay Rule (Clay)
rules.body: Colour in Clay is material, not type. Every clay that carries words carries Clay Ink (6.07:1 to 15.8:1); the only light text is on ink clay (the FPS meter) and on the footer's Wrap. Pink is the accent as a fill, an underline, a bead, or a coil, never as running text; Purple and the side-wall shades carry no words at all. A new clay surface takes ink, or takes no text.

rules.name: The Heading Slot Rule
rules.body: Headings in shared components never hardcode a family. They use the heading slot (`--font-heading`) so a world can swap the voice in one token. A world's own stylesheet (`src/styles/worlds/<world>.css`) may name its faces directly, because those classes never render outside it.

rules.name: The Loud Display, Quiet Body Rule
rules.body: Identity lives in the display size and face. Body and label sizes stay between 0.75rem and 1.125rem in every world, except Tape's condensed body at 1.1875rem and its 1.25rem skill rows, which set the same measure a regular face sets at 1rem, Cartoon's credit results at 1.1875rem, and Clay's running copy at 1.0625rem, its lede at 1.25rem.

rules.name: The One Size Rule (Engineer)
rules.body: Engineer sets everything in Courier Prime at the text size except the hero's name and role. Hierarchy is numbering, position, a 3ch indent, and bold, never size.

rules.name: The Credits Rule (Cartoon)
rules.body: A credit sets the name in the lettering over its function in small caps. A sub-credit adds its employer as a second small-caps line; a figure is billed the same way, the number as the name and what it counts beneath. Nothing labels a title from above.

rules.name: The Lettered Rule (Cartoon)
rules.body: Display text is hand-lettered per letter (fixed tilt and rise patterns, offset by a seed per title so neighbours differ) and words never break inside. The letters are drawn for the eye and hidden from assistive tech; the whole text is read once from an `sr-only` span.

rules.name: The Same Bones Rule
rules.body: Section order, container widths, and the About, Education, Projects, and Contact structures stay shared by default. A world forks a section only when its identity needs it: every world forks Hero, Experience, and Skills; Editorial also stages its own About and footer (its own Contact was retired on 2026-10-11 at the user's request, so it uses the shared one); Engineer, Terminal, Tape, Cartoon, and Clay stage their own About, Education, Projects, Contact, and footer, plus their own section headings in Experience and Skills (since 2026-10-11, when the user decided to keep the worlds and differentiate them). A fork lives inside the shared section, so anchors stay unique: the shared markup carries `data-design-hide="<world> <world>"` (space-separated) and the world's version `data-design-show="<world>"`. A world's own extras (Engineer's seams and pager) sit in `HomePage.astro` behind `data-design-show`.

rules.name: The 896 Rule
rules.body: Section content lives in an 896px column. Only the header and the hero widen to 1152px. Engineer narrows the whole page, hero included, to a 72ch column, the width of a plain-text draft. Cartoon's fields run full bleed, but their content keeps the column; only the shorts widen to 1024px for three tilted cards. Clay keeps the 896px column for every section; only its hero widens to 1152px, with the set running full width behind it.

rules.name: The Paper on Paper Rule (Cartoon)
rules.body: Depth in Cartoon comes only from one cut shape lying over another. A card, ticket, short, or figure never casts a shadow, takes a gradient, or blurs what is behind it; a new layer earns its place by overlapping.

rules.name: The Lit Clay Rule (Clay)
rules.body: A clay surface is always the full recipe: its clay colour, the surface tile under hard-light, the lift insets, and a soft cast in the sweep's teal. Never a flat clay, a black shadow, or a hard offset shadow; never a gradient standing in for the light.

rules.name: The Two-Radius Rule
rules.body: A world declares exactly two radii, `--radius-card` and `--radius-btn`. Chips, tags, and filters borrow the button radius; containers borrow the card radius.

rules.name: The Holes Are Data Rule (Tape)
rules.body: Every punched strip encodes real text, one column per character in its ASCII bits (channel 1 at the bottom, the feed hole between channels 3 and 4), via `TapeStrip`. A blank leader carries feed holes only. Never draw random holes.

rules.name: The Hand-Cut Rule (Cartoon)
rules.body: Inside the cards nothing is machine-true: edges, rules, tickets, tags, and bullets are cut or drawn, with unequal corners and wandering lines. The iris is the only true circle, because it is the camera's, not the paper's.

rules.name: The Pressed by Hand Rule (Clay)
rules.body: No clay surface has four equal corners or sits dead level. Slabs, windows, keycaps, notes, and folders take unequal radii, and slabs and notes a small tilt; only rolled pieces (beads, coils, commits, pills) are round.

rules.name: The Keycap Rule (Clay)
rules.body: Every control in Clay is a clay keycap: a face in its clay over a side wall of the same clay in shade, and a press that sinks the face into the wall by `translate` alone, on twos, never by changing colour alone or by reflowing. An action that sends is an Enter key with its return glyph; a toggle prints its plus or minus.

rules.name: The Dev Objects Rule (Clay)
rules.body: Everything on the sweep is an object from a developer's desk, pressed in clay: keycaps, editor windows, a git branch, a keyboard, sticky notes, folders, tags. Film-set grammar (slates, takes, clapperboards, wraps, frame counters) is retired at the user's request; the stop-motion lives only in how things move.

rules.name: The On Twos Rule (Clay)
rules.body: Clay moves like stop-motion: every animation is `steps()` or a 12 fps clock, poses held, never tweened; the set renders only on that clock and only while seen.

dos: Do declare a new world with the nine color tokens, two font slots, and two radii on its `[data-design]` selector (overriding `--on-accent` or `--accent-text` only if its accent misses 4.5:1, and adding world-only tokens only for its own material), register it in `src/data/designs.ts`, add its `design.<id>` name in both locales, and add it to the anti-FOUC allowlist and both visibility selector lists in `global.css`.
Do keep the accent on buttons, labels, rules, and states (The One Accent Rule), and set text on an accent fill with `text-on-accent`, never a hardcoded white or page color.

Do treat Signal Orange as a display color: rules, outlines, fills with Ink text, and text at 24px and up through `.text-accent-display`. Small orange text goes through `--accent-text` (Signal Orange Ink, #bf3900); raw Signal Orange measures 3.0:1 on Newsprint and 3.3:1 under white text.
Do keep Tape Orange off text inside a White window (2.79:1); set window copy in Tape Black ink and let orange underline or rule there (The Window Ink Rule).
Do resolve headings through the heading slot and body through the body slot in shared components; a world's own classes live in `src/styles/worlds/<world>.css` and may name its faces there.
Do render both locales in every text node behind `data-lang-show` so the language toggle never re-renders.
Do respect `prefers-reduced-motion`, and make new motion join the reveal grammar (fade, 30px rise, 0.5s, once) or the world's own signature.
Do fork a shared section only when a world's identity needs it, inside the shared section with `data-design-hide` / `data-design-show` (The Same Bones Rule).
Do carry state as a mark or a word as well as a colour (Tape's band and cross, Terminal's "●" and "Present", `aria-pressed`, `aria-expanded`).
Do give a new Cartoon card a field, a text colour, a safe colour, and a display colour from the measured pairs (The Field Rule), and keep Paper on Vermilion to display type (3.4:1).
Do animate Cartoon on held poses (`steps()`), never tweened, and keep its depth to overlap (The Paper on Paper Rule).
Do mount a WebGL scene only while its world is active, calibrate a lighter phone build, and ship a fallback, as Avant-garde (a CSS fallback) and Clay (the copy alone on the sweep) do.
Do set Clay's chrome on Sweep Raised (#14b2a7) in Sweep Shadow (5.44:1) or Clay Ink (6.67:1), with Sweep Line borders, as the design switcher does.

Do set every word on clay in Clay Ink and keep Pink a fill, an underline, a bead, or a coil (The Ink on Clay Rule); build a new clay surface from the full Lit Clay recipe and press it by hand (unequal radii, a small tilt).

Do make a new Clay control a clay keycap with its side wall that sinks on twos (The Keycap Rule), give a new Clay surface its own patch of the tile (`--tx`, `--ty`, `--ts`), and give a new Clay animation `steps()` or the 12 fps clock (The On Twos Rule).
donts: Don't mix tokens across worlds. No candy surface in Engineer, no Creative shadow in Editorial, no prompt green outside Terminal, no Tape Orange outside Tape, no Cartoon field outside Cartoon (The Own Palette Rule).
Don't fork content per world. Copy, data, order, and links come from `src/data` and `src/i18n` only; a world may restage them, never rewrite or reorder them.
Don't add a fill to Engineer beyond the Email key and reverse video, or a size beyond the text size and the hero title (The Reverse Video Rule, The One Size Rule).
Don't punch decorative noise into Tape: every strip encodes its text (The Holes Are Data Rule).

Don't give a Cartoon card a shadow, a gradient, a blur, a frame, halftone dots, or comic-book lettering effects: it is cut paper, not a comic page or a neo-brutalist card. Strokes stay drawn lines on tickets and tags in the card's own colour.
Don't label a Cartoon title from above; a credit is the name over its function in small caps (The Credits Rule).

Don't set Pink text anywhere in Clay (1.02:1 on the sweep), cast a black or hard-offset shadow, lay a flat untextured clay, or tween a Clay motion; and don't bring back film-set grammar (slates, takes, wraps) or drift into the isometric low-poly dev room: it is a developer's desk, handmade, on one painted sweep (The Dev Objects Rule).
